gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 10 build is the narrowest honest place to keep the virtio core slice reviewable without claiming deeper transport behavior.
The closure validator keeps the current virtio tranche machine-checkable, so the core lane should participate in that same evidence packet instead of relying on a slice note alone.

The live core helper already covers status sequencing, bounded feature negotiation, queue callback bookkeeping, descriptor-shape metadata, config-change bookkeeping, and driver-binding bookkeeping in memory only.
Dedicated virtio-core tests already replay the bounded handshake, queue bookkeeping, config-change, and driver-binding branches, so the survey should anchor itself to that shipped test surface.
The core slice note records the bounded implementation surface and keeps the lane honest about what still remains out of scope in drivers/virtio/virtio.c.
A dedicated survey gate prevents the closure bundle from treating the virtio core slice as implicit while the adjacent Phase 10 lanes already use manifest-backed survey records.
The lane needs a Phase 10 note that compares the landed core starter against the remaining roadmap gap and states the next bounded follow-up without widening into ring or MMIO work.

The live helper already models config-change enable, disable, pending, and flush bookkeeping, which makes the later virtio_config_enable() and virtio_config_disable() review surface concrete without claiming real locks or transport callbacks.

The live helper already records whether a bound driver exposes config_changed, which mirrors the drv && drv->config_changed branch closely enough for review without pretending probe or remove lifecycle parity.

The live helper now records bounded config-generation increments, the last observed generation, and pending-generation visibility beside the existing config-change bookkeeping, making one more core-local review surface concrete before any ring, MMIO, probe, or remove work.

The live helper now records whether __virtio_config_changed() deferred delivery, invoked a present config_changed handler, or ignored the change because no handler was bound, which makes the last config-change branch outcome reviewable without claiming probe, remove, or transport-backed lifecycle parity.

Broader virtio.c parity still mixes probe, remove, reset, and transport-backed device lifecycle paths, which remain too wide to claim even after the landed config-generation summary helper because that broader lifecycle still crosses risky transport state.
